findings.title: Validation helpers behave as documented
findings.description:
I checked the coercion and validation paths against the code in `validation.py` and the new modules. `require_iterable_of` and `require_instance` give the index-naming messages that the tests for `declarations.py` and `signals.py` expect. The edge cases hold:
- `as_integer` rejects `bool`, `np.bool_`, `Decimal`, NaN, infinity, `2.0**63` and out-of-range ints, and returns `None` for each.
- `as_real` catches the `OverflowError` from `float(10**400)`.
- `_require_time_order` and `_require_confidence_in_range` work on empty event tuples, because empty-array slicing and `.any()` are safe.
- `InvalidParametersError` passes its single `issues` argument to `super().__init__`, so copy and pickle rebuild it, and the tests cover that.

findings.title: Assertion used for type narrowing in production code
findings.description: `_require_series` follows `require_instance` with `assert isinstance(series, Series)` to narrow the type for the checker. `require_instance` already raises on a non-`Series` value, so the assert is redundant at runtime. It is also stripped under `python -O`. This is harmless, but a `cast` or a typed return from `require_instance` would avoid putting an assert in production code.

findings.title: Structural AST tests and duplicated loop-node constant
findings.description: `test_confidence.py` and `test_labels.py` each define the same `ELEMENT_LOOP_NODES` tuple and the same AST walk. These tests check implementation shape (no loops) rather than behavior. The design rule, "one vectorized expression", is only enforced this way. Moving the tuple and walk into `conftest.py` or a small helper would remove the duplication. Several test helpers also annotate their return type as bare `np.ndarray` (`_array`, `_mask` in `test_confidence.py`). Under the strict pyright setting these should be `NDArray[...]`.

findings.title: Multiple classes per file
findings.description: The Python rules ask for one class per file for models and services. `declarations.py` holds seven related types, and `display.py`, `signals.py` and `labels.py` also group related types. The file stays under 300 lines and the types are small and cohesive, so this is acceptable. Treat it as a deliberate grouping of tiny related types rather than a violation to fix.
